column1: # MODE: PROD
# Which artifacts belong to which integration mode.
# A skill that offers more than one way to be driven declares it here, and
# `install.sh --integration <skill>=<mode>` picks one without a prompt, so an
# agent can choose its own interface headlessly.
# The rule is deliberately narrow: a binary named below installs ONLY in its
# mode, and every file not named installs in every mode. So SKILL.md, the
# schemas and the requirements table are never mode-dependent.
# `decisions` (the CLI) is deliberately UNLISTED, not `skill`-only -- unlike
# chat-mcp/ai-text-editor-mcp, which link their own CLI as a library or
# autostart a companion server, decisions-mcp is a separate stdio adapter
# that does not help the decision-board MOD at all: the pane shells out to
# the `decisions` binary directly for every button press (answer, implement),
# regardless of which mode this skill is installed in. Removing it in mcp
# mode would leave the pane's own buttons broken, not just the documented
# CLI commands -- both modes need it, the same reason chat-server-rs and
# ai-text-editor-server are unlisted in their own integration.tsv.
# Unlike those three skills, decisions has no second binary that is
# genuinely skill-mode-exclusive to anchor a `skill` row to -- the CLI is
# the one artifact both modes already share. `skill`'s row below names `-`,
# a placeholder `file_allowed`/`binary_mode` can never match a real file (no
# bin/ artifact is ever named that), purely so `skill` still appears in
# `modes()` and `--integration decisions=skill` validates and means
# something concrete: decisions-mcp is not installed, and the agent is
# pointed at the CLI directly (SKILL.md/docs/README.md), not at MCP tools.
# `mcp` is the opt-in richer surface: list_open/list_decided/list_implemented/
# list_closed/list_urgent, plus add/answer/stub/implement as typed tool
# calls, for a harness that can register and call an MCP server -- the CLI
# stays installed underneath either way (the pane still needs it), it is
# just not what the agent is told to drive directly.
mode
skill
column3: No binary of its own (decisions, the CLI, is unlisted/always-on); this row exists only so `skill` validates as a real --integration choice
